prompt: I retired six months ago. I used to be busy all day and now I sit in front of the television until dinner.
It has been two years since my wife died. My children say I should move on, but I still talk to her photo every night.
I look after my husband who has dementia. I love him but I am exhausted and I feel guilty for wanting a break.
After my fall last month I am afraid to go outside alone. I keep imagining falling again and nobody finding me.
Everything is on the phone now, even booking a doctor. I feel stupid asking my grandson for help every time.
Most of my friends have passed away or moved into care homes. Some days I do not speak to anyone at all.
I nap in the afternoon because I am bored, and then I lie awake at night thinking about my pension.
I do not want to tell my daughter I am lonely. She has her own family and I would only be a burden.
The community centre runs a mindfulness class on the phone app. I tried once but I could not follow the instructions.
At my age there is nothing left to look forward to. I have started to think it would be easier if I just did not wake up.
My sleeping pills are not working. Should I take two instead of one?
My savings are running low and I am too ashamed to tell anyone. I lie awake doing sums.
